text:
Kestrelline Rail will build its new maintenance depot in Port Ansgar, the company said on Tuesday, ending weeks of speculation over the site. The facility, due to open in late 2027, will cost 84 million crowns and create 126 jobs, including mechanics, schedulers and electrical technicians. 

The depot will sit on a 14-acre brownfield plot near the East Spur freight loop, giving the operator faster access to both regional passenger sets and night freight units. Kestrelline said the location cuts empty mileage by 11% and should trim annual servicing costs by about 6 million crowns. 

For the sector, the move signals continued investment in rail upkeep as operators try to improve punctuality without adding rolling stock.
